candidate_windows.window_text: In this section, we will briefly introduce reinforcement learning for LLMs as well as the DPO algorithm, and then discuss the methodology of LongReward, including multi-dimensional LLM scoring for long-context-based model responses and the combination of LongReward and DPO.

We conduct experiments on two latest open-source base models, namely Llama-3.1-8B (Vavekanand and Sam, 2024) and GLM-4-9B (Zeng et al., 2024), which have been continually pre-trained on extensive long texts and support a context window of 128k tokens. We first supervisedly fine-tune these two models, then conduct DPO experiment with LongReward, as described in Sec. 3.3. All models are trained using Megatron-LM library (Shoeybi et al., 2019) on 4 nodes with $8 \times \mathrm{H}800$ GPUs.

Supervised Fine-tuning. We adopt the method of Bai et al. (2024) to construct the long-context

SFT dataset. Specifically, we collect 10k documents from the pre-training corpus of GLM-4 (Zeng et al., 2024), covering 9 varied domains. These documents are mainly in English and Chinese and their lengths range from 8k to 64k tokens. For each document, we employ GLM-4 to propose a QA pair via Self-Instruct (Wang et al., 2023), where different task type descriptions such as summarization and information extraction are incorporated into the prompts to guarantee the diversity of generated queries. Following Bai et al. (2024), we mixed this dataset with 76k general SFT instances from ShareGPT (Chiang et al., 2023) and fine-tune Llama-3.1-8B and GLM-4-9B in the mixed dataset for 1,800 steps (approximately 2 epochs), with a learning rate of 1e-5 and a batch size of 8.

Direct Preference Optimization. We follow the pipeline described in Sec. 3.3 to construct the preference datasets, using prompts from the long-context SFT dataset and taking GLM-4 as $M_{\mathrm{judge}}$ . For each prompt, we sample 10 candidate responses. We adopt Zhipu-Embedding-2† as the retriever for the assessment of faithfulness and retrieve top-5 context chunks for each factual statement. For DPO training, we set $\beta$ and $\lambda$ to be 0.15 and 0.1, respectively. We use a learning rate of 1e-6 and a batch size of 16, and train from the SFT checkpoints for around 400 to 800 steps.

Besides the SFT models, we consider the following long-context preference data generation policies as baselines: Short-context reward model (SRM). This policy utilizes the short-context reward model trained by Hou et al. (2024) to construct preference datasets, where we ignore the context and only feed the query and response into the reward model due to its limited context window. Contrast with larger models (Contrast). This policy uses responses generated by GLM-4 and the SFT model as the winning and losing responses, respectively, based on the observation that larger LLMs typically generate better responses. In addition, we also report the performance of officially post-trained models, i.e., Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and GLM-4-9B-Chat, as references. Long-context benchmarks. We use two bilingual benchmarks LongBench-Chat (Bai et al., 2024) and LongBench (Bai et al., 2023) for the evaluation of long-context capacities, where the former is a small-scale dataset that evaluates models' long-context alignment proficiency on 50 real-ward queries, and the latter is a comprehensive benchmark that tests general long-context understanding abilities. We conduct evaluations on three types of tasks within LongBench: Single-Doc QA, MultiDoc QA, and Summarization (each task includes 4 sub-datasets), including 2,350 instances in total. Following Bai et al. (2024) and (Zhang et al., 2024), we ask GPT-4o to automatically rate the models' responses based on the query and groundtruth answers via few-shot (for LongBench-Chat) or zero-shot prompting (for LongBench). In addition, we also conduct human evaluation in Sec. 4.4 and 4.7 to further validate the effectiveness of LongReward and its agreement with human preference.

Short-context benchmarks. We select two short-

context benchmarks MT-Bench (Zheng et al., 2023) and AlpacaEval2 (Dubois et al., 2024) to investigate whether LongReward will influence models' ability to follow short instructions. MT-Bench covers 8 categories with 80 questions and uses GPT-4 to rate model responses on a scale of 1-10, while AlpacaEval2 consists of 805 questions from 5 datasets and employs GPT-4-turbo to measure models' length-controlled win rate against GPT-4-turbo. More detailed statistics of the evaluation datasets are listed in Table 1.
